text.p: The lira closed easier at 106,000 against the dollar on Friday after Thursday's 105,780 due to banks' continuing dollar demand despite central bank's dollar sales, bankers said.
Turkish central bank sold dollars for lira to banks towards the close on Friday in an attempt to restraint the U.S. currency's rise fuelled by persistent demand.
The lira firmed to 106,000 against the dollar after the intervention from previous 106,180. It had opened at 106,100.

Bankers said dollar demand picked up in the last few days as several banks attempted to close their end-year currency positions and importers' foreign currency demand also rose, as a sual at end-year.
The central bank had carried out two minor interventions by selling dollars earlier this week, on Monday and Thursday.

Bankers said the downgrading of Turkey's long-term foreign currency rating to "B plus" from "BB minus" by European rating agency IBCA did not affect the market much as the lira had already weakened to 106,170 at midday.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 105,700 lira at the opening, up from Thursday's 105,450 lira close, but later lowered it to 105,650 due to a weaker dollar in world markets.
The money market opened 9.6 trillion lira short.

Overnight money traded at 77.50 and 77.75 percent in the day and the central bank funded 43.7 trillion lira at 78 percent overnight in the afternoon. It had drained 7.1 trillion lira at 57 percent yesterday when the average money rate was 58.73 pct.

The central bank also lent banks 27.5 trillion lira via t/n value deals at 74 percent, down from the 28.4 trillion lira it funded on Wednesday. It also lent 2.2 trillion lira at 75 percent via tomorrow/week value deals.
Bond market yields firmed around a point on tightening liquidity.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper firmed to 112.29 percent from Thursday's 110.99. The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 112.78, up from Thursday's 111.39 percent average.
